```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(interfacespace)
```

## 1. The workbook in brief

A mixed methods evaluation produces findings from qualitative work (strand
`Q`) and from numbers (strand `N`), and states claims that join them. The
interface space keeps what was found, what is claimed and what was decided in
separate tables, with the links between them written down:

| Table | Content |
|---|---|
| agents | who did the work: persons, models, algorithms |
| findings | one checkable result per row, with strand and where to check it |
| transformations | a finding made from other findings (counting a theme, comparing themes across groups defined by a measure) |
| claims | headline claims, with the findings they rest on and the fit of the strands (`confirm`, `expand`, `discord`, `single-strand`) |
| relations | links among claims: `backs`, `clashes`, `covers` |
| decisions | endorse or reject, with actor, date, rows and a written reason |

Four rules govern the tables.

1. Every row is born a candidate. Status changes only through decisions.
2. A decision needs a person as actor and a written reason. Decisions are
   never edited or deleted; a later decision on the same row supersedes an
   earlier one.
3. A row proposed by a model enters as a candidate and cannot be endorsed in
   the call that creates it.
4. Endorsing means accepting a row as correctly recorded. Whether a claim is
   joint is computed, not decided: a claim is joint when its findings, traced
   back through endorsed transformations to their roots, include at least one
   `Q` and one `N` root.

A transformation passes on the roots of its inputs, so a theme plus the
percentage computed from that same theme has one root, not two. The
exception is coding rule 12: when qualitative data are compared across groups
defined by a quantitative measure, the output finding is a root of its own
strand as well (`partition = TRUE`).

```{r synthetic}
x <- InterfaceSpace$new("example")
x$add_agent("A1", "Analyst", "person", "Author of the decisions")
x$add_agent("A2", "LLM extractor", "model", "model x, prompt v1")
x$add_finding("F1", "Q", "Participants report growing confidence.",
              where_to_check = "Interviews, p. 7", proposed_by = "A2")
x$add_finding("F2", "N", "Confidence theme present in 68% of interviews.",
              where_to_check = "Table 3", proposed_by = "A2")
x$add_finding("F3", "N", "Career adaptability rises, d = 0.45.",
              where_to_check = "CAAS scale, T0-T2", proposed_by = "A2")
x$add_transformation("F2", made_from = "F1", method = "theme counted",
                     done_by = "A1", proposed_by = "A2")
x$propose_claim("C1", "Coaching raises confidence.",
                rests_on = c("F1", "F2"), fit = "confirm", proposed_by = "A2")
x$propose_claim("C2", "Coaching raises confidence and adaptability.",
                rests_on = c("F1", "F3"), fit = "confirm", proposed_by = "A2")
x$decide(c("F1", "F2", "F3", "T:F2", "C1", "C2"), "endorse", actor = "A1",
         reason = "Recorded as stated in the report.")
x$claims()[, .(code, rests_on, fit, status, joint)]
x$roots()
```

`C1` looks mixed but has one root (`F1`); `C2` is joint.

## 2. A published register: Woodall et al. (2018)

The package ships the registers of ten published evaluations. The register
of Woodall et al. (2018), a social prescribing service evaluated with a
pre/post questionnaire and interviews (study `HLT-C2`), is read with
`read_register()`, which adds every row as a candidate and replays the
decision log in order.

```{r read}
hlt <- read_register(bundled_registers("HLT-C2"))
hlt
head(hlt$decisions()[, .(code, action, rows, reason)], 4)
```

### Joint claims

```{r joint}
cl <- hlt$claims("endorsed")
cl[, .N, by = .(joint, fit)]
cl[joint == TRUE, .(code, claim, rests_on, fit)]
```

### Joint display

For each joint claim, the qualitative and quantitative roots side by side.

```{r display}
jd <- hlt$joint_display()
knitr::kable(jd[, .(claim, q_findings, n_findings, fit)])
```

### Counts

Counts use endorsed rows only.

```{r counts}
hlt$counts()[, .(claims, joint, related, related_share, relations, covers,
                 backs, clashes, unsupported_claims)]
```

`validate()` lists violations of the register rules; an empty table means
none were found.

```{r validate}
hlt$validate()
```

## 3. All ten registers

```{r all}
cnt <- register_counts(bundled_registers(), pooled = TRUE)
knitr::kable(cnt[, .(study, claims, joint, related, related_share,
                     relations, clashes, unsupported_claims)])
```

The coding protocol, the prompts and a data dictionary are in
`system.file("extdata", package = "interfacespace")`.
